newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends easy, gilts hog limelight.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends easy, gilts hog limelight.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed lower at 1.00-1.50 percent against the day's opening levels of 1.50-2.00 percent, dealers said.
The easy money conditions and covered positions kept the call rates below 2.0 percent level, a dealer said.
"Today's repo auction won't have much effect on call money market, which will rule below the 2.0 percent levels for the rest of the fortnight," he said.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said it set a cut-off rate of 3.60 percent at a four-day repo auction on Monday, unchanged from the previous week.
The RBI said it received and accepted 17 bids for 62.50 billion rupees.
The easy money conditions and the lack of other avenues to park the funds led to prices of securities rising by a hefty 50 paise, a dealer said.
The 12.50 percent government stock 2004 rose to 102.30 rupees against the previous of 101.90 rupees.
The zero coupon bond maturing in 2000 rose by 20 paise to 73.50 rupees and the 13.80 percent 2002 stock rose to 107.35 rupees from 107.00 rupees, dealers said.
The long term maturity paper 13.05 percent 2007 jumped to 104.25 rupees from the previous 103.75 rupees, a dealer said.
Yield on treasury bills maturing in April 1998 fell to 7.95 percent against the previous 8.00 percent, he said
